question: Which of the following animals have two-chambered heart?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Fishes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of chambers in an animal's heart is a key factor in determining the efficiency of its circulatory system. 
 
• Two-Chambered Heart
 
 
• Fish: Fish have the simplest heart structure, consisting of two chambers: one atrium and one ventricle.
 
• Function: Blood is pumped from the heart to the gills for oxygenation and then directly to the rest of the body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Three-Chambered Heart
 
• Amphibians and most reptiles: These animals have a three-chambered heart with two atria and one ventricle.
 
• Function: Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix to some extent in the single ventricle, which can reduce the efficiency of oxygen delivery to tissues.
 
• Four-Chambered Heart
 
• Birds and mammals: These animals have a four-chambered heart with two atria and two ventricles.
 
• Function: This highly efficient heart completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, ensuring optimal oxygen delivery to tissues.
 
• Why do chamber numbers matter?
 
 
• Efficient oxygenation: More chambers allow for more efficient separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, leading to better oxygen delivery to tissues.
 
• Metabolic needs: Animals with higher metabolic rates, like birds and mammals, require more efficient oxygen delivery.
